title: Alerts and Badges
summary: An alert is a message box. A badge is a small label, often used for a count or a short status.
introduction: An alert is a message box. A badge is a small label, often used for a count or a short status. Make a clear reminder and a book-count badge. Use words to explain the meaning, so colour is never the only clue.
learningObjectives: Create alerts in every contextual colour with the right ARIA role
Add headings, links and a dismiss button that works with the bundle
Attach badges to headings, buttons and links for counts and statuses
Keep alerts and badges readable and accessible

blocks.text: An alert is a `<div>` with `.alert` and one contextual class: `alert-primary`, `alert-secondary`, `alert-success`, `alert-danger`, `alert-warning`, `alert-info`, `alert-light` or `alert-dark`. Each gets a pale background, a matching border and dark text of the same hue; in 5.3 these come from the `*-bg-subtle`, `*-border-subtle` and `*-text-emphasis` variables, so they also adapt to dark mode. Add `role="alert"` so screen readers announce the message as soon as it appears.

blocks.title: Four contextual alerts
blocks.code:
Your profile has been updated.
Payment received. Thank you!
Your subscription ends in 3 days.
The file could not be uploaded.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
Four full-width rounded boxes, each with 1rem padding, a 1px border and 1rem space below it:
Primary: pale blue background, dark blue text
Success: pale green background, dark green text
Warning: pale yellow background, dark brown text
Danger: pale red background, dark red text

blocks.text: Headings, links and rules inside an alert

Longer messages can hold a heading, several paragraphs and links. `alert-heading` makes a heading inherit the alert's colour, `alert-link` makes a link bold in the matching emphasis colour, and an `<hr>` inside an alert takes the same hue. Put `mb-0` on the last paragraph so the alert's own padding is the only space at the bottom.

blocks.title: A richer alert
blocks.code:
Order confirmed

Your seeds will ship within two working days. You can track the parcel from your orders page.

Questions? Reply to the confirmation email.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content: A pale green box containing a 24px dark green heading, a paragraph in which "your orders page" is bold dark green, a thin green rule, and a final paragraph with no extra space below it

blocks.text: To let the user close an alert, add `alert-dismissible` (which reserves space on the right), the classes `fade show` (so it fades out instead of vanishing), and a `btn-close` button with `data-bs-dismiss="alert"`. The close button is an empty element, so its `aria-label` is the only text a screen reader has. The bundle must be loaded: when the button is clicked, Bootstrap removes the `show` class, waits for the fade, then removes the alert from the DOM entirely.

blocks.title: An alert with a close button
blocks.code: Heads up! Your password expires tomorrow.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
A pale yellow box with "Heads up!" in bold, extra padding on the right and a small × button in the top-right corner
Clicking × (bundle required) fades the alert out over 150ms and removes it from the page; it does not come back until the page reloads

blocks.title: Common mistake: a close button that does nothing
blocks.text: The × renders fine without JavaScript, which hides the real problem: the click only works when `bootstrap.bundle.min.js` is loaded **and** the button carries `data-bs-dismiss="alert"`. The Bootstrap 4 spelling `data-dismiss` is ignored. A second trap is leaving out `alert-dismissible`: the alert still closes, but the message text runs underneath the button because no space was reserved for it.

A badge is an inline label: `.badge` sets small bold text (75% of the parent's font size), tight padding and rounded corners, and `text-bg-{colour}` gives it a background **and** a text colour that contrasts with it. Because the size is relative, the same badge is large in an `<h1>` and small in a paragraph. `rounded-pill` makes the ends fully round, the usual look for counts and statuses.

blocks.title: Badges in headings, text and buttons
blocks.code:
Inbox New

Status: Active

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
"Inbox" with a grey rounded label "New" beside it, three quarters of the heading's size (30px on wide screens)
"Status:" followed by a small green pill reading "Active"
A blue button "Messages" with a small light grey label "4" inside it
A blue button "Alerts" with a red pill "9+" overlapping its top-right corner; a screen reader reads "Alerts 9+ unread alerts"

blocks.text: The last badge shows the positioning recipe: `position-relative` on the button, then `position-absolute top-0 start-100 translate-middle` on the badge, which puts the badge's centre exactly on the button's top-right corner. The `visually-hidden` span matters: "9+" alone means nothing to someone who cannot see where the badge sits.

Prefer `text-bg-*` over the older `bg-*` on badges. `badge bg-warning` or `badge bg-light` keeps the badge's default white text, which is unreadable on yellow or near-white; `text-bg-warning` switches the text to black automatically, just as the button variants do.

rows: Tell the user the result of an action
Announced immediately, large enough to notice
Label a status next to an item
Compact, scales with the surrounding text
Show a count on a button or tab
Badge inside the button, with hidden text
Visually attached to the control it describes
A short message that disappears on its own
Alerts stay until dismissed; toasts time out

blocks.title: Colour is not enough
blocks.text: Red and green alone do not tell a colour-blind user which alert is good news. Start the message with a word that says so ("Saved", "Error") or add an icon; Bootstrap Icons is a separate package you can include for that.

questions.question: Which attribute makes a screen reader announce an alert as soon as it appears?
questions.explanation: role="alert" marks the element as a live region with assertive politeness, so its content is read out immediately. The other attributes are not valid for this purpose.

questions.question: A `.badge` inside an `<h1>` is rendered larger than the same badge inside a paragraph.
questions.explanation: Badges use a font-size of .75em, so they scale with their parent: 75% of the heading size in an h1, 75% of 16px in a paragraph.
